A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete text, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved into v5's expanded appendices.

before.justification: V4 reports original MLLM accuracy, consistency, correction-method evaluations, and table-extraction analyses in Experiments 1–3.

after.justification: V5 retains those empirical experiments and adds model evaluations, specialized extractor comparisons, CoT experiments, and manual error analyses.

M1.justification: The six correction pipelines in Section 2.2 remain unchanged. Appendix F adds optional zero-shot Chain-of-Thought variants of table-based QA and visualization redrawing, changing answer generation to include intermediate reasoning.

E1.justification: Table 1 retains the same datasets, question types, and chart/misleader coverage. Appendix C adds an image-free evaluation scenario using self-contained real-world questions, testing answers based on parametric knowledge without the chart.

E2.justification: Appendix E/Table 3 adds DePlot and MatCha as evaluated alternatives to MLLM table extraction. Appendix F also evaluates CoT alone and alongside correction methods. These introduce substantive comparator classes absent from v4's reported correction comparisons; DePlot and MatCha were previously cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: V5 expands the reported model panel from 18 to 19, adding Claude-3.5-Sonnet. New protocols include selecting and rephrasing 22 questions for an image-removal control, testing CoT variants, manually evaluating random samples of 30 misleading visualizations, and inspecting extraction across the ten most frequent misleaders.

E4.justification: Appendices C and F–I add parametric-knowledge and CoT analyses, direct extraction-versus-QA audits, extraction accuracy by misleader, and axes-error analysis. Two new extraction case studies cover 3D effects and dual axes. V4's CHARTOM consistency analysis and inverted-axis example are retained and relocated.

E5.justification: Section 3.2 changes the paired t-test from two-sided to one-sided, retaining the 0.05 threshold. Section 2.3 removes the stated seed of 42. Standard-deviation reporting and the two-sided McNemar test remain; neither PDF establishes additional repeated runs.

E6.justification: Figure 4 retains the original 18 models' scores and adds Claude, changing mean misleading-chart accuracy from 25.6% to 26.4% across different model panels. New results include GPT4o's 77% with-image versus 50% image-free accuracy, DePlot/MatCha comparisons, CoT outcomes, and manual extraction scores. Some appendix baseline values in Table 3/Figure 11 do not reconcile with the retained main correction plot, without an explained setting change.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theory, proofs, or derivations. The misleader definitions in Table 2 are unchanged; revisions to statistical testing concern empirical evaluation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the novelty framing from introducing six correction methods to providing their first comparison or analysis, and expand the stated study from 18 to 19 MLLMs. The central vulnerability claim and reported effectiveness of table-based QA and redrawing remain.

C2.justification: V5 substantially expands explanations of correction failures: incorrect tables can yield correct answers for the wrong reason, accurate axes may be ignored, and specialized extractors may struggle with unfamiliar chart types. It adds CoT-specific tradeoffs, more precise extraction failure conditions, and discussion of dataset size and representativeness.

D1.justification: Appendix B supplies explicit extraction, redrawing, and QA prompts previously absent. V5 discloses two A100 GPUs and adds dataset licensing, research-use restrictions, and CHARTOM access instructions. These materially expand reproducibility information, although the earlier implementation paragraph's explicit API-access details are omitted.

R1.justification: Section 4 explicitly credits Liu et al. (2023a,b) with introducing table-based QA and positions its use against misleading charts as an application of that approach. Those works were already cited in v4. Anthropic (2024) and Wei et al. (2022) are added; several other reference changes merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: V5 tightens prose, shortens the conclusion, adds an ethics statement, and moves selected detailed discussions into dedicated appendices. The main section sequence and three-experiment narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V5 adds four prompt figures, a CoT comparison figure, two extraction examples, and Tables 3–6. V4's misleader heatmap and inverted-axis example move to v5 Figures 12 and 13. Figure 4 gains Claude, and the document receives substantial typography and page-layout changes.

improvement.justification: V4's explanation of extraction bottlenecks relied largely on paired-table mismatch, and its correction comparison lacked specialized extractor and CoT controls. V5 adds direct extraction-versus-QA audits, those relevant comparisons, and explicit prompts, substantially strengthening the central empirical argument and reproducibility. The unexplained switch to one-sided testing and inconsistencies between new appendix values and the retained correction plot limit confidence in some details, but do not outweigh these gains.
